title: Joining in 1937 and the amalgamation of Local 767 into 47
summary: She joined around 1937; on amalgamation in the 1950s members kept seniority, received a $1,000 death benefit and the old assets passed to 47.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Uh-huh. What year was it you joined the union, do you remember?
It was -- it must have been about 1937. It was -- because I've been a life member for a long time now.

And the one nice thing, the one thing I have to say, the benefit, when the union finally -- when the unions, rather, when they amalgamated, part of the bargain was for us to maintain our -- I was going to say seniority, we'll

use that word. You know, your membership standing. Whatever time you had spent or put in, that would go with your new record, with your record, over to 47. So -- and then they also had a policy, 47 had a policy, where you'd have a $1,000.00 death benefit, so we inherited that also. We turned over all the assets from the old union, which was a building -- which was a building and maybe a couple of pianos or something like that. And this piece of property, of course, wasn't a very -- wasn't a valuable piece of property. It was in a business neighborhood, you know. But all of the assets were turned over, so all of the members became -- we were recognized as full members of 47, with the death benefit shared by the other members.
Did the negotiations take a long time? It seems like I remember a lot of fund raising and campaigning at the time of working for the amalgamation.

Well, I wasn't here at the time this happened. This was in the '50s when it happened, and I wasn't here at that time. See, I was travelling at the time, and I missed all of that, but there was an awful lot and there are a lot of people, several people that really should bet credit. Marl Young and Buddy Collette and Benny Carter and Red Callendar. And these guys were, you know, they were very, very instrumental in really getting the show on the road. And it was something that would have had to happen in later years, and that was really the time for it to happen.
